body:
hi there  -

I'm not deeply familiar with the real world scenarios by which CancelledError occurs but the conditions being created here also occur if you use the NullPool, which does not pool any connection:

```python
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool


engine = create_async_engine(
    "postgresql+asyncpg://scott:tiger@localhost/test",
    future=True,
    poolclass=NullPool,
)
```

that pool class is literally just connect() / close().   so I don't know what options we have here if the task is completely cancelled and GC does not seem to be closing out connections.

The asyncpg connections here are no longer referenced in any way that SQLAlchemy has access to, and they should be garbage collected.  Some initial attempts to trace out exactly what happens in this test case seem to indicate there's no point at which SQLAlchemy could intercept these connections to .close() them, we have a garbage collection hook on them and even that is not getting called.

I have a feeling you could make this program with asyncpg directly pretty easily and im not sure why asyncpg doesn't close out connections that should be garbage collected.     their docs give no guidance: https://magicstack.github.io/asyncpg/current/search.html?q=cancellederror&check_keywords=yes&area=default

so far, wihtin the "finally:" of the block, the asyncpg connection itself can be "closed", which seems to let asyncpg let go of it, but we still are not given any opportunity to do any pool cleanup.   this happens in a plain vanilla asyncio program as well

```python
import asyncio
from asyncio import current_task

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool


engine = create_async_engine(
    "postgresql+asyncpg://scott:tiger@localhost/test",
    future=True,
    poolclass=NullPool,
)

async def get_and_cancel():
    conn = await engine.connect()
    try:
        await conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT 1")
        current_task().cancel()
    finally:

        print("we can close the asyncpg connection directly")
        asyncpg_conn = (await conn.get_raw_connection()).connection._connection
        print("and we get here, and we can close it out")
        await asyncpg_conn.close()

        print("but we dont get here, which is where the above is supposed to happen")
        await conn.close()

async def main():
    while True:
        try:
            await get_and_cancel()
        except asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError:
            pass


asyncio.run(main())
```


plain demo:

```python
import asyncio

from asyncio import current_task
import asyncpg


async def get_and_cancel():
    conn = await asyncpg.connect(user="scott", password="tiger", host="localhost", database="test")
    try:
        result = await conn.fetch("SELECT 1")
        current_task().cancel()
    finally:
        # we get here, and this seems to change the state of asyncpg
        # so that the error is not raised
        await conn.close()

        # but we never get here
        import pdb
        pdb.set_trace()


async def main():
    while True:
        try:
            await get_and_cancel()
        except asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError:
            pass


asyncio.run(main())
```
related issue but this was fixed: https://github.com/MagicStack/asyncpg/issues/464

here we are, this also throws the error, using asycnpg only, we are closing the connection, but because we have to emit a ROLLBACK (or do anything with an await whatsoever), we are blocked:

```python
import asyncio

from asyncio import current_task
import asyncpg


async def get_and_cancel():
    conn = await asyncpg.connect(
        user="scott", password="tiger", host="localhost", database="test"
    )
    try:
        result = await conn.fetch("SELECT 1")
        current_task().cancel()
    finally:
        await conn.fetch("ROLLBACK")
        await conn.close()


async def main():
    while True:
        try:
            await get_and_cancel()
        except asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError:
            pass


asyncio.run(main())
```
i've added https://github.com/MagicStack/asyncpg/issues/772 as a demo and maybe they can tell us what we should do in this kind of case.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**ensure greenlet_spawn propagates BaseException** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2876

figured out that the greenlet spawn was not allowing us to handle BaseException fully.    This issue still has things I don't understand very well (why the asyncpg connections are not garbage collected, why it is so hard to get cancel() to do something predictable in a unit test) but this seems to be what's needed to make sure our invalidation code handles invalidating the connection.

issue.title: Explicit exception in context manager
issue.body:
bare except statement are frowned upon
prefer explicit except BaseException


### Description
- session_scope context manager uses bare `except`
- This doesn't seems to be a good practice https://github.com/PyCQA/flake8-bugbear#list-of-warnings
- Instead of using `Exception` and changing the behavior prefer usage of `BaseException` 
- This should rollback the commits if `KeyboardInterrupt` or similar exceptions raise https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44655854/what-is-the-difference-between-except-and-except-baseexception/63169967#63169967

### Checklist


This pull request is:

- [x] A documentation / typographical error fix
	- Good to go, no issue or tests are needed

**Have a nice day!**
